asparagus-fresh-cooked-fat-added-ns-as-t.title: Asparagus, fresh, cooked, fat added, NS as to fat type

content.title: About
content.content: Asparagus is the young shoot of the herbaceous plant Asparagus officinalis. Fresh asparagus is commonly prepared by steaming, boiling, sautéing, or roasting, often with a small amount of oil or butter added to enhance flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus is one of the first spring vegetables to appear after winter.
There are three main varieties: green, white (grown in darkness), and purple.
In ancient Rome, asparagus was a luxury food and a status symbol.
It provides more vitamin K than most other vegetables.
Asparagus can be used as a side dish, in salads, soups, and even desserts.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Asparagus supplies folate (B9), vitamin B6, and thiamine, which support metabolism and nervous‑system health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A 100 g serving contains about 20 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: It contains glutathione, vitamin C, and carotenoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber in asparagus promotes regular bowel movements and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Mineral source
items.content: Asparagus provides potassium, iron, and copper, important for electrolyte balance and blood formation.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to asparagus, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Asparagus contains oxalates, which in excess can contribute to kidney‑stone formation.

items.title: Food interactions
items.content: Large amounts of asparagus may affect the action of certain medications, like anticoagulants, due to its vitamin K content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Trim the tough ends, wash the spears, and steam, boil, or quickly sauté them in a little oil or butter for 3‑5 minutes. Adding butter or olive oil improves taste but raises the calorie count.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store asparagus in the refrigerator wrapped in a damp paper towel in the vegetable drawer, and use within 3‑4 days. Do not wash before storing to avoid excess moisture.

content.title: About
content.content: Burrito, meat, no cheese is a classic Mexican dish consisting of a large soft wheat tortilla filled with sautéed meat, rice, beans, vegetables and sauces, but without cheese. This combination keeps the dish lighter while preserving the rich flavor of the meat and aromatic spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat flour was more available than corn.
Traditional meat is slow‑cooked in adobo sauce, giving the dish its distinctive aroma.
Leaving out cheese makes the burrito suitable for people with lactose intolerance.
In the United States burritos are often served with guacamole, salsa and sour cream, though the original version may omit these toppings.
Burritos are portable – they can be wrapped in foil and eaten on the go.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice and beans supply slowly digestible carbs that help maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Beans and vegetables add fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and beans contain B6, B12 and niacin, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish provides iron, zinc and magnesium, which aid immunity and metabolic processes.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sauces and seasonings can be salty, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Large portions can be high in calories due to rice and cooking oil.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat tortillas contain gluten, posing a risk for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Potential pathogens
items.content: Undercooked meat may harbor bacteria, so it should be cooked thoroughly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos are hand‑held. Warm them in a microwave or skillet, add fresh salsa, guacamole or a squeeze of lime. For extra crunch you can include lettuce leaves.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, freeze it – up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.

cream-half-and-half-fat-free.title: Cream, Half and Half, Fat Free

content.title: About
content.content: Fat‑free half‑and‑half cream is a blend of milk and cream with a very low fat content (usually 0.5‑1 %). It is used as a lighter alternative to regular cream, providing a creamy texture without the extra calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Commonly used in diet cooking because of its low fat content.
Retains much of the milk flavor despite the reduced fat.
Works well as a base for sauces, soups, and desserts without needing additional fat.
In some markets it is sold under the name “Half‑and‑Half” even when completely fat‑free.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Provides far fewer calories than regular cream, helping with energy balance.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Like milk, it supplies calcium important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Small amounts of lactose can promote beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains lactose, so those with intolerance should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Some brands add stabilizers or emulsifiers; check the label if you are sensitive to these ingredients.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Use it for sauces, soups, purees, baking, and desserts. It can be whipped, but the foam will be less dense than with regular cream. Pairs well with berries, fruits, and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store refrigerated at 1 °C‑4 °C. After opening, consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑color.

content.title: About
content.content: Crisp "Peach" is a crunchy dried snack made from whole peaches, dried at low temperature. The snack retains the natural aroma and sweetness of ripe peach, offering a light texture and bright fruit flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peaches belong to the Rosaceae family and are relatives of plums, cherries, and apricots.
Low‑temperature drying preserves up to 90 % of vitamin C, which is usually lost in conventional drying.
Crisp "Peach" contains no added sugar – the sweetness is completely natural.
The snack is easy to transport and store, requiring no refrigeration.
Natural peaches contain more than 200 bioactive compounds, many of which remain in the product.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Peaches are a good source of vitamin C, which supports immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A, beneficial for vision and skin health.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids normal digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The snack is virtually fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Peaches contain flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Peach allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peaches, ranging from skin rashes to severe symptoms.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although no added sugar is present, natural sugars may be a concern for people with diabetes; moderation is advised.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: During long storage, antioxidants may be used; check the label for unwanted additives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crisp "Peach" is convenient as a standalone snack, added to granola, yogurt, salads, or used in baking for a fruity note.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. For extended storage, keep refrigerated to preserve aroma and crunch.

content.title: About
content.content: Cod (Gadus morhua) is a marine fish from the cod family that lives in cold northern Atlantic waters. Its flesh is white, flaky, and mildly flavored, rich in protein and low in fat. Cod is commonly baked, broiled, or grilled, and is also used in soups and stews.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cod is one of the world’s most important commercial fish species, with annual catches exceeding 5 million tonnes.
Wild cod can grow over 2 m long and weigh more than 100 kg, though most market fish are much smaller.
Cod contains low levels of mercury, making it a safe choice for frequent consumption.
The fish can change its skin coloration to blend with its surroundings, helping it avoid predators.
Cod is the primary ingredient in many fish sticks and processed fish fillets.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 18 g of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Cod is low in saturated fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: While lower than fatty fish, cod still supplies EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in vitamin B12, niacin (B3), and B6, which aid nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, important for thyroid health and bone strength.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cod.

items.title: Contamination
items.content: Occasionally cod can contain trace amounts of heavy metals or microplastics; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large portions may cause discomfort for people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cod can be baked with herbs and lemon, broiled on a grill, steamed, or added to soups. Fillets are easy to portion, marinate, or bread. Pair with vegetables, potatoes, or whole grains for a balanced meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh cod in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic, and use within 2 days. Frozen cod should be stored at –18 °C and consumed within 3‑4 months. Before cooking, check for a mild sea scent; discard if it smells strong or ammonia‑like.

content.title: About
content.content: Beef hot dog is a sausage made from ground beef, seasoned with spices and placed in a soft bun. It is a popular fast‑food item often served with mustard, ketchup, pickles, and onions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The beef hot dog appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as a cheaper alternative to the traditional pork version.
In some U.S. regions (e.g., Chicago) a distinct style is served without ketchup but with mustard, pickles, and tomato relish.
The bun is usually baked with milk and butter, giving it a soft, slightly sweet texture.
Beef sausage typically contains about 15‑20 % fat, which keeps the product juicy.
In several countries the hot dog is considered a national snack, such as Japan where it is often topped with teriyaki sauce.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: A beef hot dog provides roughly 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Zinc
items.content: Beef provides zinc, which supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and modest fat helps promote a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed sausages often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Beef hot dogs contain saturated fats that, when eaten frequently, may contribute to cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some versions include nitrites and other preservatives that are considered undesirable in large amounts.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may be allergic to beef or to the spices used in the sausage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the hot dog in a split bun, adding mustard, ketchup, mayo, pickles, onions, or cheese to taste. It can be cooked on a grill, skillet, or microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 3‑4 days. Frozen versions last up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.

hot-dog-sandwich-beef-on-wheat-bun.title: Hot Dog Sandwich, Beef, on Wheat Bun

content.title: About
content.content: A hot dog sandwich with beef on a wheat bun is a classic fast‑food item: a juicy beef patty placed inside a soft wheat bun, often topped with mustard, ketchup, pickles, and onions. It is a popular snack in the United States and many other countries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hot dog appeared in the late 19th century and quickly became a street food in New York.
Traditionally hot dogs are eaten with the hands, without knives or forks.
The United States celebrates National Hot Dog Day on July 23.
A wheat bun provides a softer texture compared to the classic white bun.
Beef patties for hot dogs are usually grilled or pan‑fried.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The beef patty is a rich source of complete protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Beef contains easily absorbable heme iron, important for blood formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef provides vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Carbohydrates from the bun
items.content: The wheat bun supplies a quick source of energy through complex carbohydrates.

items.title: Dietary fiber (when using whole‑grain wheat bun)
items.content: A whole‑grain wheat bun adds dietary fiber, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Beef patties can contain significant saturated fat, which may increase cardiovascular risk if consumed in excess.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Ketchup, mustard, and pickles often add a lot of sodium, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The wheat bun contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Hot dogs are calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on a weight‑management diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hot dogs are typically eaten by hand, holding the bun from the bottom. Common toppings include mustard, ketchup, mayonnaise, pickles, onions, cheese, or lettuce, according to personal preference.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared hot dogs can be stored in the refrigerator for 2–3 days in an airtight container. Keep the bun in a dry place to prevent it from becoming soggy. When reheating, use an oven or grill rather than a microwave to retain a crisp crust.

content.title: About
content.content: Strawberry milk with reduced sugar is a dairy‑based beverage flavored with natural strawberry extract and lightly sweetened with sugar substitutes. It retains the creamy taste of milk and a subtle berry note while containing far less sugar than conventional fruit‑flavored milks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The strawberry flavor is derived from real strawberries, not artificial aromatics.
Sugar reduction is achieved using stevia and erythritol, which do not raise blood glucose.
The drink is fortified with calcium and vitamin D, just like regular milk.
It suits people watching their sugar intake but is not completely carb‑free.
Packaging is often made from recyclable plastic to lower environmental impact.

items.title: Low Sugar Content
items.content: Reduced sugar helps control calorie intake and supports stable blood glucose levels.

items.title: Rich in Calcium
items.content: Provides a good source of calcium essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Probiotics (in some versions)
items.content: Certain formulations include live cultures that promote gut health.

items.title: Low‑Calorie Snack
items.content: Ideal as a light snack or breakfast addition, delivering energy without excess calories.

items.title: Lactose Intolerance
items.content: Contains lactose, so those with intolerance should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Milk Allergy
items.content: People allergic to milk proteins may experience reactions.

items.title: Artificial Sweeteners
items.content: While stevia and erythritol are generally safe, they can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in some individuals.

items.title: Residual Sugar
items.content: The product still contains a small amount of sugar; strict low‑sugar diets should account for it.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy strawberry reduced‑sugar milk chilled, add it to smoothies, oatmeal, cereal, or use as a base for desserts. It pairs well with bananas, berries, and nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 1 °C–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as texture may change.

content.title: About
content.content: The California sushi roll is a popular Western-style roll made with sushi rice, nori, crab meat (or imitation crab), avocado, and cucumber. It is typically served with soy sauce, wasabi, and pickled ginger. The roll is known for its mild flavor and creamy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The roll was created in the 1970s at a California restaurant using imitation crab to keep costs low.
Avocado gives the roll its characteristic buttery taste and adds nutritional value.
The California roll is considered a “Western” adaptation of traditional Japanese sushi, tailored to American palates.
Some variations replace crab with salmon or tuna, but the classic recipe keeps the original ingredients.
Wasabi is often omitted to let the delicate avocado flavor shine.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Avocado provides monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E from avocado acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Cucumber and rice supply fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The roll contains virtually no added sugar, making it suitable for moderate consumption.

items.title: Provides protein
items.content: Crab meat (or its imitation) adds protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Crab meat can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce served with the roll is often high in salt; low‑sodium options are recommended.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: If stored at improper temperatures, the rice can become a breeding ground for bacteria.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite its light appearance, the combination of rice, avocado, and crab imitation makes the roll fairly calorie‑dense.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: California rolls are usually eaten with chopsticks, dipped in soy sauce. Add a touch of wasabi if desired and eat pickled ginger between bites to cleanse the palate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rolls in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C, wrapped in plastic film or placed in an airtight container. Consume within 24 hours to maintain rice freshness and nori crispness.
